📝 Notes
Mar 10, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint Notes by Gemini 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Module design sketches were reviewed, and a Mycelium prototype demonstrated, with a unified goal needed for concrete development.Safety Document Review PostponedThe discussion of safety regulations was postponed until Friday to allow for more time to review the recently received final safety requirements document. The current Wednesday meeting will now focus exclusively on modules, and a Friday 2 PM safety meeting will be scheduled.Module Sketch Review and FeedbackLatest module sketches presented two organization approaches: a chat-accessible text-heavy option and a journey-based 'maps' view. Participants suggested using the 'Open' app for design inspiration to ensure the content organization reflects the interrelation between concepts.Mycelium Prototype and GoalA Mycelium prototype was demonstrated, which aims to save bookmarks and cluster knowledge using a 'brain' initialized with a specific prompt. The team agreed on the necessity of defining a singular, unified, and small goal for Mycelium to create a complete end-to-end pipeline.
Details
Schedule and Safety Document Review: The participants agreed to postpone the discussion of safety regulations to a meeting on Friday to allow more time for review, as the final safety requirements document was recently sent by Melissa (00:00:00) (00:04:28). The Wednesday meeting will now focus exclusively on modules (00:02:52). Amir Houieh committed to having their sketches ready around 5 or 6 and also committed to reviewing the safety documents before Friday (00:00:00).
Upcoming Safety Meeting Logistics: Noémi Biró volunteered to schedule the separate safety meeting with Melissa for Friday, proposing it around 2 PM, which Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh indicated would provide enough time to read and digest the safety documents (00:02:52) (00:05:40). The goal for this meeting is to provide input on the best way to tackle the safety requirements and outline actionable points (00:04:28).
Module Sketching and Design Concepts: Noémi Biró shared their latest module sketches, which explored two distinct ways of organizing content: a text-heavy approach accessible via a chat option, and a thematic 'maps' view based on the user's journey, such as "six weeks after loss" (00:05:40). The journey-based view allows the user's path to grow incrementally and provides access to relevant sessions and suggestions for daily focus (00:07:38).
Feedback on Module Organization and Design: Gabor Kerekes suggested reviewing the design of the "Open" app for inspiration, specifically focusing on its interface and content organization patterns, as they have good design and structure their content into modules (00:10:25). Gabor Kerekes also expressed a preference for the design to reflect the interrelation and overlap between concepts like mind and body, to avoid boxing things in too cleanly (00:13:14).
Demonstration of Mycelium Prototype and Brain Initialization: Amir Houieh shared a quick test of a Mycelium prototype that attempted to save bookmarks and connect them to a 'brain' for processing and knowledge clustering (00:16:51). This brain is initialized with a specific prompt and uses both a cloud model for prompt decomposition and a smaller model for the rest of the process, though the demo encountered an error due to running out of credit (00:20:24).
Search for Concrete Scenarios for Mycelium Development: Amir Houieh expressed the need for a more concrete scenario or real data to truly test the Mycelium prototype, suggesting they need more direction rather than exploring abstract problems (00:24:19) (00:29:55). Gabor Kerekes suggested using Amir Houieh's personal friction point—the daily context switching between apps—as a natural angle for development, prioritizing building something functional that meets daily workflow needs (00:26:03) (00:32:20).
Establishing a Unified Goal for Mycelium: The participants discussed the importance of defining a singular, unified, and tiny goal to aim for to avoid wasting time on generalized exploration (00:29:55). They suggested focusing on making Mycelium more concrete, even if it has limited features, to create a complete end-to-end pipeline (00:33:24). Noémi Biró argued that Mycelium should not have only one use case to avoid being perceived as only a bookmarking tool. Gabor Kerekes committed to providing concrete scenarios in the next daily meeting to help narrow the focus of the project (00:34:35).
Personal Well-being and Administrative Tasks: Amir Houieh mentioned feeling close to a mental breakdown and affirmed they should watch out for their well-being, though they noted that work can sometimes help. Before concluding the meeting, Amir Houieh also noted the need to work on the proposal for the minutes/administrative tasks and committed to creating a proposal (00:36:01).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will have the sketches ready around five or six.
Amir Houieh will read the safety documents before Friday.
Noémi Biró will send an invite to Melissa for a meeting on Friday to discuss the safety regulations.
Noémi Biró will sketch out what happens when going inside one of the modules and different exercises like a body check or five senses.
Amir Houieh will sketch the type of exercise or activity that can be done using only voice or without a phone in hand.
Gabor Kerekes will look at the interface of the Open app for breathwork and meditation.
Amir Houieh will work on the minutes and make a proposal to review it together.
The group will read through the safety documents from Melissa before the Friday meeting.
